hypotheses.reasoning: First anomaly in the chain is catalog-svc PutObject to S3 us-east-1 failing with 503 SlowDown and then 500 InternalError (#124 onward). AWS SDK retry quota exhausted (#133). catalog-svc returns 500 'storage write failed' to search-api (#127, #136, #151), and search-api's 500s reach web-bff (#126...). catalog-svc request volume did not spike, the DB, redis and GC all look healthy, and no deploy shows up in the logs. That points to the provider-side S3 fault, not to our own load.

The 503 'reduce your request rate' message could be S3 throttling caused by our own request rate. But no traffic increase is visible, and the later errors are 500 InternalError, which suggests a provider problem.
One catalog.updates message went to the DLQ at 21:55, but that was isolated. index-worker kept processing normally, so this is probably a red herring.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check the AWS Health Dashboard for S3 us-east-1 and open a support case with the S3 request IDs from the logs. Take the S3 artifact write out of the synchronous GET /products/batch path: make it async or best-effort, or fail open so search still serves when the write fails. Add a circuit breaker and backoff on catalog-svc's S3 client, and consider failing over to a replica bucket in another region.
